headline: Planning Your Visit to Lake Diefenbaker’s Dunes
reservation: Vehicle entry permits are mandatory and can be purchased online or at the gatehouse. While the park remains open for day use, the demand for campsites at Douglas often exceeds supply during long weekends; check the Saskatchewan Parks reservation system for current availability and booking windows.

days.title: Active Dunes and Shorelines
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Park Gate

stops.name: Cundall Ridge
stops.detail: Hike the ridge for a panoramic view of the massive Lake Diefenbaker reservoir and the surrounding prairie.

stops.name: Sand Dunes Trail
stops.detail: Explore the unique active sand dune ecosystem, a rare geological feature in the region located at the end of a dedicated interpretive path.

days.driving: Internal travel is minimal; allow 15 minutes between trailheads.
days.note: Walking on the dunes can be strenuous in the midday sun; bring ample water.

days.title: Qu'Appelle Valley Vistas

stops.name: Douglas Park Beach
stops.detail: Enjoy the expansive sandy beach and swimming area, which serves as the primary recreation hub for the park.

stops.name: Trans Canada Trail Segment
stops.detail: Walk a portion of the national trail that winds through the park, offering views of the diverse grassland birds.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for the short drive from the village of Elbow; conditions vary.
days.note: Beach conditions can change with the water level of the reservoir; check local signage.

days.title: Inland Sea Exploration
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from the Boat Launch

stops.name: Lake Diefenbaker Marina
stops.detail: Observe the scale of the Gardiner Dam project and the recreational boating activity that defines the region.

stops.name: Sunset Point
stops.detail: A quiet spot near the campground loops perfect for viewing the vast sky over the water.

days.driving: Allow 10 minutes between the marina and camping areas.
days.note: High winds are common on Lake Diefenbaker and can affect water activities.

intel.title: Beachfront Access
intel.text: The main beach parking lot is large but fills quickly on hot Saturday afternoons. Arrive early or use the overflow areas designated by park staff.

intel.title: Nearby Services
intel.text: There is no fuel station inside the park boundaries. The town of Elbow, located a short drive north, is the primary source for gasoline and groceries.

intel.title: Connectivity
intel.text: Mobile signal is generally strong near the park office and main beach. Expect some dead zones while hiking deeper into the dune fields.

intel.title: Dune Temperatures
intel.text: The sand dunes retain heat significantly during the summer months. Plan dune walks for early morning to avoid the most intense heat of the day.

intel.title: Water Levels
intel.text: As a reservoir, water levels in Lake Diefenbaker can fluctuate seasonally. This may impact the size of the beach and boat launch accessibility; check the Water Security Agency for updates.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at Saskatoon Airport, drive south on Highway 11, and stop in Davidson or Elbow for final supplies before entering the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard sedans and RVs are perfectly suitable for the paved and well-maintained gravel roads within the park.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Cundall Ridge provides a dramatic view as the light reflects off the reservoir.
